# Jito stake pool and JitoSOL — facts

> Source-anchored units about Jito stake pool and JitoSOL: 8 across 4 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-06 · 8 units · 4 sources · rights: quote -->

## Structure and components

- [statement] The Steward program (part of StakeNet) is an Anchor program that holds the staking authority of the SPL stake pool, scores validators from on-chain Validator History data, keeps target stake on the winners, and re-evaluates the set on a fixed cadence. Its core operations are permissionless, so any cranker can run them, and its parameters are set through Jito DAO governance. (high confidence) — https://www.jito.network/docs/stakenet/introduction · keywords: Jito stake pool and JitoSOL · also: https://chainflow.io/jito-stakenet/

## How it works

- [statement] In the Steward code (master branch), the Config account holds an admin key that can change the parameters and blacklist authorities, call SPL stake pool instructions that need the staker signature, and pause or reset the state machine. Separate authorities set parameters, edit the blacklist, change priority-fee parameters, and manage directed staking (meta upload, whitelist, ticket override). Scoring and rebalancing are permissionless: Jito says any cranker can run them. Because the admin can pass through staker-signed calls, the admin key could steer delegation outside the scoring rules (an inference from the code description, not a documented behaviour). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jito-foundation/stakenet/master/programs/steward/src/state/accounts.rs · keywords: Jito stake pool and JitoSOL · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jito-foundation/stakenet/master/programs/steward/README.md, https://www.jito.network/docs/stakenet/introduction

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Jito's FAQ describes MEV and priority-fee distribution through TipRouter: an end-of-epoch snapshot builds a merkle tree of tips for validators and their stakers pro rata, operators vote on the root (more than 2/3 agreement), and a cranker uploads it. It states a 3% protocol fee on MEV and a 1.5% fee on priority-fee distributions. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-10-11) — https://www.jito.network/docs/jitosol/faqs/technical-faqs/ · keywords: Jito stake pool and JitoSOL
- [statement] Direct unstaking through Jito takes up to one epoch (about 2-3 days at most) and costs the 0.1% withdrawal fee; selling on Jupiter or another DEX is instant at a variable spread. For stake-account deposits, the Interceptor program holds the minted JitoSOL for 10 hours; claiming early costs a fee that falls linearly from about 10% to 0%. The fee detail is in the FAQ only; the glossary confirms the 10-hour cooldown. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-10-11) — https://www.jito.network/docs/jitosol/faqs/technical-faqs/ · keywords: Jito stake pool and JitoSOL · also: https://www.jito.network/docs/jitosol/resources/jitosol-glossary/
- [statement] JIP-16 required validators to share at least 50% of priority fees to qualify for JitoSOL delegation (per Jito's StakeNet governance page). JIP-25 paused deployment because priority fees had fallen about 72% since the JIP-16 vote (Blockworks data cited by the proposal). The README shows the priority-fee filters disabled by parameters (priority_fee_scoring_start_epoch = 65535). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.jito.network/docs/stakenet/governance/ · keywords: Jito stake pool and JitoSOL · also: https://forum.jito.network/t/jip-25-expand-the-validator-set-and-modify-jito-stake-pool-eligibility-and-ranking-criteria/877, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jito-foundation/stakenet/master/programs/steward/README.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Steward scoring runs every 10 epochs using a 30-epoch lookback. Inputs named by the independent Chainflow write-up are voting performance, commission, MEV commission and superminority rank, drawn from vote accounts, tip-distribution accounts and gossip data. Severe underperformance or a commission rug triggers immediate unstake and redelegation instead of waiting for the next cycle. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-10-11) — https://chainflow.io/jito-stakenet/ · keywords: Jito stake pool and JitoSOL · also: https://www.jito.network/docs/jitosol/faqs/technical-faqs/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] JitoSOL is built on Solana Labs' SPL Stake Pool program, which handles pooling, delegation and token minting. Jito's glossary says that underlying program has had nine audits. (medium confidence) — https://www.jito.network/docs/jitosol/resources/jitosol-glossary/ · keywords: Jito stake pool and JitoSOL · also: https://www.jito.network/docs/jitosol/faqs/technical-faqs/
- [statement] Jito's docs say slashing 'does not really exist right now on Solana' and is 'currently not implemented', yet list slashing and stake pool bugs as ways the rate could fall. They also say the pool is non-custodial and that holders could withdraw SOL and rewards even if Jito disappeared. These are Jito's statements; this pass did not check whether Solana slashing has since activated. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-10-11) — https://www.jito.network/docs/jitosol/faqs/technical-faqs/ · keywords: Jito stake pool and JitoSOL · also: https://www.jito.network/docs/jitosol/resources/jitosol-glossary/, https://www.jito.network/docs/jitosol/jitosol-liquid-staking/security/overview/
